title: Displacement Addressing: Base, Index and the Same Arithmetic Under Three Names
quickIdea: One formula, EA = A + [R], covers indexed, base-register and PC-relative addressing. What changes is which part is fixed and what the register is being used to mean.
remember: Effective address = address field + contents of a register. Two parts: one fixed in the instruction, one that can change.
Indexed: the register holds an offset (an index), the field holds a base address. Arrays, A[i].
Base register: the register holds the base address, the field holds a displacement. Records, structure fields, and a relocatable segment.
Base with index: two registers plus a displacement. The most general form, and the one that costs the most bits.
PC-relative is displacement addressing with the program counter as the register; the field is a signed offset in words or bytes.
One operand memory reference in every one of these forms - the address arithmetic is not a memory read.
The register is not modified by the address computation, which is what separates these modes from autoincrement and autodecrement.

example.prompt: A struct is at the address in R1 and its grade field is 400 bytes in. Separately, an int array A starts at 1000 and each element is 4 bytes. Give the effective addresses for A[7] and for grade, and name the mode each needs.
example.work: A[7] = 1000 + 7 x 4 = 1028, which is base-plus-index with the base 1000 in the instruction and the index 7 in a register (scaled). grade = [R1] + 400, which is base-plus-displacement with 400 fixed in the instruction and the base in the register.
example.answer: 1028 by base-with-index; [R1] + 400 by base-with-displacement. The array's index varies at run time; the record's displacement does not.

gateAngle: GATE has asked this form three times and named it differently each time. GATE CSE 2011 Q.21 calls 20(R2) 'Base Indexed Addressing' and accepts that; GATE CSE 2017 Set 1 Q.11 calls X(R1) 'Index addressing mode' and accepts that; GATE CSE 2026 Set 1 Q.4 pairs base-with-index with an array element and base-with-displacement with a record element. The safe reading is the formula EA = A + [R] plus the question 'does the register or the constant change?' - the naming is the paper's, not a fact to memorise.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: A 16-bit two's complement displacement field is added to a base register. What range of fields can it express, and is that enough for a 1 MB structure?
variations.answer: -32768 to +32767 bytes, which covers the first 32 KB of the structure and nothing beyond.
variations.why: The 2017 Set 1 question turns on exactly this: 400 bytes fits comfortably, which is part of why the displacement form is the efficient answer there.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does base-with-displacement suit a record and base-with-index suit an array?
variations.answer: A record's field offsets are known at compile time, so they can be constants in the instruction; an array's index is known only at run time, so it must come from a register.
variations.why: Which operand varies decides which operand goes in the instruction. This is the single idea behind all three displacement flavours.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: The same code is loaded at a different address. Which displacement flavour still works without change?
variations.answer: PC-relative, because both the instruction and its target moved by the same amount, so the offset is unchanged. Base-with-displacement works too, provided the base register is reloaded.
variations.why: This is the bridge to the relocation card, and the reason GATE's 1998 and 2004 relocation questions give different answers to what look like the same question.

trap.what: Trying to decide whether a form like 20(R2) is 'indexed' or 'base' from the notation.
trap.why: The notation is identical. Only the intent - which operand is fixed and which varies - separates them, and different papers use the names differently.
trap.counterexample: GATE accepted 'Base Indexed' for 20(R2) in 2011 and 'Index addressing mode' for X(R1) in 2017. Both are EA = A + [R]. Answer the arithmetic, then answer the paper's label.

check.question: R4 = 2000 and the instruction holds 12. What is the effective address, and how many memory reads does the operand take?
check.answer: EA = 2012, and one memory read for the operand.
check.explanation: The addition is done in the address unit, not in memory. Only the final fetch of M[2012] touches memory.

sourceLine: The two-part address of displacement addressing - one part fixed in the instruction and one part held in a register that can change - is the last thing read from Deka et al., Lecture 12 (English, read in part). The statement that the control steps differ by mode and that address arithmetic happens in the address unit: Deka et al., Lecture 18 (English, read in part). The translated three-way split of displacement addressing into relative, base-register and indexing, with base register holding a memory address and index holding a positive displacement: computernetworksite.in (Hindi, translated, read in part). The three GATE answers are recomputed in scripts/validate.py.
